articles.title: Pearlmark Provides $81M for Apartment Project in Coral Gables
articles.narrative: Empira Group has secured an $81 million construction loan from Pearlmark for the development of Aurelian, a 12-story, 160-unit multifamily project in Coral Gables, FL. The project, designed by Behar Font & Partners, will feature extensive amenities including a swimming pool, fitness center, coworking space, and a public park. Empira Group previously acquired the 1.2-acre site in 2025 for $18 million and recently broke ground on the development, which is slated for completion in 2028.

data_points.notable_features: The 12-story building will include 248 parking spaces, a swimming pool, a fitness center, a yoga studio, coworking space, an entertainment lounge, a pet grooming station, and a 6,000-square-foot public park.
data_points.project_notes: The 1.2-acre site was previously acquired for $18 million in 2025.

articles.title: Citi Provides $210M Refi for Grand Hyatt Resort in Southern California
articles.narrative: Trinity Investments has secured $210 million in refinancing for the Grand Hyatt Indian Wells Resort & Villas, a 531-key luxury hotel in Southern California's Coachella Valley. Citi provided the five-year, floating-rate, single-asset, single-borrower CMBS loan, which follows a $62 million renovation and rebranding of the property in 2024. The successful refinancing highlights a growing lender appetite for recently repositioned hospitality assets with strong sponsorship in supply-constrained markets.

data_points.notable_features: 45-acre resort with nine swimming pools, a water park, a 30,000-square-foot spa, six restaurants and bars, and tennis and pickleball courts.

articles.title: L.A. Industrial Vacancy Falls for First Time in Two Years
articles.narrative: The Los Angeles County industrial market experienced its first annual decline in vacancy in two years during the third quarter, driven by 1.9 million square feet of positive net absorption. This marks the fourth consecutive quarter of positive absorption, bringing the year-to-date total to 5.1 million square feet. Demand was particularly strong for larger warehouses, while smaller properties continued to struggle with negative absorption. Despite improving occupancy, average direct asking rents remained flat, still significantly below peak levels from 2023.
articles.market_intelligence: Los Angeles County's industrial market saw its vacancy rate fall 20 basis points quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year to 5 percent. Leasing activity increased 6.5 percent year-over-year but declined 15.7 percent from the second quarter. Average direct asking rents held steady at $1.19 per square foot per month, which is 4 percent below the average from a year ago and 30.4 percent below the Q3 2023 peak of $1.71 per square foot. Central L.A. led in absorption with 1.11 million square feet, while the South Bay was the most active leasing market with 4.46 million square feet of transactions. The construction pipeline expanded for the first time since early 2025.

articles.title: Skin Care Brand FaceGym to Open New Tribeca Location at 110 Reade Street
articles.narrative: FaceGym, a skin care brand specializing in "facial fitness" studios, has signed a 10-year lease for 2,400 square feet at 110 Reade Street in Tribeca, New York City. The new location is expected to open in October 2026. The landlord's broker noted that Tribeca has become a prime destination for luxury wellness and beauty, making it an ideal fit for FaceGym's brand identity and customer engagement strategy.

data_points.address: 110 Reade Street, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Six-story, mixed-use residential property with ground-floor retail, located near the corner of Reade Street and West Broadway.
data_points.project_notes: Former retail tenant was Pure Barre, a fitness studio.

articles.title: Greenheck Group to Open 1.3 MSF Manufacturing Facility in Owasso, Oklahoma
articles.narrative: Greenheck Group, a manufacturer of commercial air movement equipment, is establishing a 1.3 million-square-foot manufacturing facility in Owasso, Oklahoma. The company acquired a 72-acre former Macy's distribution campus for the project, which represents a $300 million capital investment and is expected to create approximately 700 new jobs over the next five years. Initial building improvements are slated for completion by spring 2027, with production commencing soon after.

data_points.project_notes: Expected to generate 700 new jobs over five years. Initial building upfit improvements by spring 2027, with production beginning shortly thereafter.

articles.title: HPI Breaks Ground on 396-Unit Multifamily Project in North Austin
articles.narrative: HPI Real Estate Services & Investments has commenced construction on The Kent, a 396-unit multifamily development in North Austin, near The Domain. The seven-story apartment project is being developed in partnership with private investors and is expected to be completed by mid-2029.

articles.title: Stream Realty Partners Nears Completion of 215,891 SF Industrial Project in Spring, Texas
articles.narrative: Stream Realty Partners is nearing completion of Summit Grove Business Park, a 215,891-square-foot industrial project in Spring, Texas. Building One, a 124,930-square-foot rear-load facility, is currently available for lease. Building Two, comprising 90,961 square feet, has been fully preleased to an energy services company, indicating strong demand for industrial space in the northern Houston submarket.

data_points.notable_features: Building One is a 124,930-square-foot, rear-load structure. Building Two is a 90,961-square-foot facility.

articles.title: TexAmericas Center Signs MOU to Support Japanese Manufacturing, Business Growth in Texarkana
articles.narrative: TexAmericas Center has entered into a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with AIST Solutions, a Japanese industrial, research, and engineering firm, and its American subsidiary. This agreement aims to foster manufacturing and business expansion for Japanese companies seeking to enter or grow within the U.S. market, leveraging TexAmericas Center's 12,000-acre mixed-use and industrial park near the Arkansas-Texas border.

articles.title: Newmark Arranges $76.2M in Bridge Financing for New Orlando Multifamily Community
articles.narrative: Newmark has arranged $76.2 million in construction take-out bridge financing for Citron at The Packing District, a 354-unit multifamily community in Orlando. The financing was secured on behalf of EMBREY, the landlord of the property. The community, delivered in 2025, is part of the larger $700 million Packing District mixed-use redevelopment.

data_points.notable_features: Amenities include a top-floor deck with a media room, resort-style swimming pool with lounge and poolside cabanas, a Wi-Fi lounge with a conference room and micro-offices, and an adjoining six-story structured parking garage.
data_points.project_notes: The multifamily community is situated within the 202-acre, $700 million Packing District mixed-use redevelopment.

articles.title: Marcus & Millichap closes sale of 16-unit multifamily community in Wausau
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap has facilitated the sale of The Reserve at Greenwood Hills, a 16-unit luxury multifamily community in Wausau, Wisconsin, for $5,525,000. The transaction also included a fully entitled, shovel-ready development site approved for an additional 48 units. Both the seller and the buyer are Wisconsin-based investors.

data_points.notable_features: Located within a master-planned golf-course community, the property offers underground parking, golf-cart access to Greenwood Hills Country Club, and resort-style amenities including a dining room, bar, theater, library, outdoor terraces, and walking trails.
data_points.project_notes: The sale included a fully entitled, shovel-ready development site for up to 48 additional units, bringing the potential total to 64 units.

articles.title: Construction work starts on 118-unit Upton apartment project in Clayton
articles.narrative: Construction has commenced on The Upton, a $55 million adaptive reuse project transforming the former 7UP world headquarters in Clayton, MO, into a 118-unit Class A residential development. Led by Revive Capital Development, with KAI Build as general contractor and HDA as architect of record, the project will preserve the Mid-Century Modern building's historic exterior while creating modern studio, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom apartments. The development aims to revitalize a long-vacant landmark and introduce extensive amenities to downtown Clayton.

data_points.notable_features: Historic rehabilitation of the 11-story Mid-Century Modern former 7UP world headquarters, featuring an elevated outdoor plaza, fitness center, club room, heated outdoor spa, theater, game room, private speakeasy, outdoor kitchens, fire pits, and a private dog park.
data_points.project_notes: The project represents a significant shift from earlier redevelopment concepts that called for replacing the existing building with a new high-rise, prioritizing historic preservation and adaptive reuse instead.

articles.title: Cravey Real Estate Services brokers sale of former car wash property in Aransas Pass
articles.narrative: DAGER Properties, LLC acquired the former Bay Car Wash property at 952 S. Commercial St. in Aransas Pass, TX, from CCC Real Estate Holding Co., LLC. The 3,496-square-foot, seven-bay car wash facility, situated on 0.64 acres at a signalized corner, had ceased operations and was returned to the lender prior to the sale. Despite challenges including a lack of operational history and significant vandalism during the marketing period, the property attracted a buyer quickly, with the new owner planning to reactivate it as a car wash operation.

articles.title: Habitat breaks ground on redevelopment of LeClaire Courts public housing community in Chicago’s Garfield Ridge
articles.narrative: Habitat and Cabrera Capital have broken ground on the first residential phase of the LeClaire Courts redevelopment, a multiphase project transforming a former public housing site in Chicago's Garfield Ridge neighborhood. This initial phase involves the construction of two six-story mixed-use buildings with 183 apartments, 90% of which will be affordable, along with a 14,000-square-foot early childhood education center and ground-floor retail. The comprehensive redevelopment aims to create a mixed-income, mixed-use community with up to 700 residential units and 440,000 square feet of commercial space, reconnecting the site with the surrounding area and providing essential services and economic opportunities.

data_points.notable_features: 90% of units designated as affordable; includes a 14,000-square-foot early childhood education center and ground-floor retail.
data_points.project_notes: Redevelopment of a former public housing community demolished in 2011. The first phase is part of a larger multiphase project that will ultimately deliver up to 700 residential units and 440,000 square feet of commercial space. Infrastructure improvements are underway across the site. Construction of the first phase is expected to be completed in 2028.

articles.title: Rich Development Trades Newly Built Shopping Center
articles.narrative: Rich Development Enterprises has sold the newly constructed Apple Valley Towne Center, an 87,042-square-foot regional shopping center in Apple Valley, CA. The property, completed in 2026, was fully leased to three national junior box tenants at the time of sale. The marketing strategy, which began before tenants opened, generated significant interest from a diverse pool of investors by offering the assets individually and as a package.

articles.title: Doug Middleton to Lead New York Institutional Capital Markets at Cushman & Wakefield
articles.narrative: Cushman & Wakefield has appointed Doug Middleton as executive vice chairman and Jack Stillwagon as executive managing director to co-lead its Institutional Capital Markets business in New York City. Both join from CBRE, bringing significant experience in sourcing and executing large commercial asset transactions across various property types, including office, residential, and industrial sectors. Their roles will also involve collaboration with national capital markets teams.

articles.title: Gilbane, Strada Development Break Ground on Affordable Tower in Castle Hill/Soundview
articles.narrative: Gilbane and Strada Development LLC have broken ground on 1920 Turnbull, a $175 million affordable and supportive housing development in the Castle Hill/Soundview neighborhood of the Bronx. The 22-story building will feature 228 affordable rental apartments, with 137 units designated for formerly homeless individuals and families. This project represents the first phase of a larger development, with a second building planned to add another 207 affordable apartments.

data_points.phase_1: 228 affordable rental apartments, including 137 permanent supportive housing units
data_points.notable_features: Includes 137 permanent supportive housing units for formerly homeless individuals and families, with a 24/7 staffed lobby, outdoor recreation space, fitness room, community room, bike storage, and laundry facilities.
data_points.project_notes: This is the first of two planned buildings; Phase 2 will add 207 additional affordable apartments, 18% of which will be supportive housing, with construction planned to begin within the next year.

articles.title: Private Event Space Planned to Top Former Hancock Center
articles.narrative: 360 CHICAGO, the observation deck at 875 North Michigan Avenue, is expanding its footprint by opening a new 14,000-square-foot private event venue, ELEVAIRE CHICAGO, on the 96th floor. This expansion, set to begin accepting bookings in 2027, is part of a larger project to create Chicago's first multi-story observation deck across three floors, increasing 360 CHICAGO's total space to over 50,000 square feet. The parent company, Magnicity, acquired the 95th and 96th floors in 2024 and has engaged the building's original architects, Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, for the design.

data_points.notable_features: Located on the 96th floor, offering sweeping views of Lake Michigan and the city skyline.
data_points.project_notes: Part of a larger expansion of 360 CHICAGO into the 95th and 96th floors, increasing its total footprint to over 50,000 square feet across three floors.

articles.title: PCCP Provides $41M Refi on North Park Multifamily
articles.narrative: PCCP has provided a $41 million senior loan to Foulger-Pratt for the refinancing of Tenney North Park, a recently completed 125-unit multifamily property in San Diego's North Park submarket. The loan replaces an existing construction loan for the eight-story building, which also includes ground-floor retail. The property offers a mix of market-rate and affordable units, benefiting from its strategic location near dining, entertainment, and major employment centers.

data_points.address: 2260 El Cajon Blvd, San Diego, CA
data_points.notable_features: Eight-story property with 115 market-rate units and 10 affordable units, averaging 727 square feet, along with 3,116 square feet of ground-floor retail and 146 parking spaces. Located near North Park's 30th Street dining and entertainment corridor, with access to Downtown San Diego, the Hillcrest healthcare cluster, and UTC/La Jolla.

articles.title: Proposition 45 Would Set Deadlines For Some Projects' CEQA Reviews
articles.narrative: Proposition 45, a ballot initiative in California, aims to establish specific deadlines for California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) reviews for certain essential projects. The proposition seeks to streamline the approval process, thereby reducing associated costs and project delays. This measure is intended to accelerate the development of critical infrastructure and other significant projects within the state.

articles.title: Wu Secures Approval To Give Tax Breaks To 4 Big Multifamily Projects
articles.narrative: Mayor Michelle Wu has secured approval from the Boston Planning & Development Agency (BPDA) to provide an estimated $31.5 million in tax breaks for four significant multifamily projects. This initiative aims to incentivize the development of approximately 1,400 new housing units across the city. The move reflects a strategic effort to address housing supply challenges and promote affordability through targeted financial incentives for developers.

data_points.project_notes: Tax breaks estimated at $31.5M approved to incentivize development.

articles.title: California Governor Candidates See Different Solutions To State's Housing Troubles
articles.narrative: California's gubernatorial candidates, Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton, are proposing distinct approaches to address the state's persistent housing affordability crisis. Their differing solutions reflect varied perspectives on how to tackle the complex issues of housing supply, cost, and accessibility for residents across the state.

articles.title: Illinois Voters Weigh Data Center Referendums On November Ballot
articles.narrative: Voters in several Illinois municipalities will consider referendums on the November ballot that could hinder data center development. These measures represent a new tool for communities to potentially control or restrict the growth of data center projects within their jurisdictions.
